You are checking a claim someone has made about a statutory provision. Your job is to REFUTE it if it can be refuted. Default to unsound when uncertain.

The claim asserts that, according to this provision, one quantity bears on another. The two most common ways such a claim is wrong:
  (a) SUBJECT MISMATCH. The provision governs something other than the quantity the claim says it determines. A provision about an insurer's duty to pay for treatment does not govern how much treatment occurred. A provision conferring jurisdiction to assess a claim does not make one assessed quantity a determinant of another.
  (b) WORD MATCHING. The claim latched onto a word rather than a meaning -- reading 'caused by the fault of the driver' (a fault condition) as being about how difficult causation is to establish.

A claim is sound only if the provision genuinely makes the first quantity bear on the second. Mentioning both is not enough. A precondition for the provision to operate is not automatically a determinant of its subject.

PROVISION: 89C Motor Accidents Compensation Act 1999

--- BEGIN PROVISION TEXT ---
89C
 
Settlement offers to be made if claim not settled
(1)
 If the parties participate in a settlement conference but the claim is not settled, each party must make an offer of settlement within 14 days after the settlement conference concludes.
(2)
 A claim cannot be referred to the Commission for assessment under this Part until each party has made the required offer of settlement.
(3)
 An offer of settlement must include a schedule of damages sufficient to explain the manner of calculation of the damages to which the offer relates.
(4)
 A party who has made the required offer of settlement can refer the claim for assessment if more than 14 days have elapsed since the settlement conference concluded and the Commission is satisfied that the other party has refused or failed to make the required offer of settlement.
s 89C:
 Ins 2007 No 95, Sch 1 [57]. Am 2020 No 18, Sch 6.7[38] [39].
--- END PROVISION TEXT ---

THE CLAIM: this provision makes 'Nature' (the procedural route: settlement approval, or damages assessment) bear on 'Legal Procedural Complexity' (an ordinal score for procedural complexity of the proceeding), as a gate.
Quoted in support: "A claim cannot be referred to the Commission for assessment under this Part until each party has made the required offer of settlement."
Mapping offered: The concept of a claim being 'referred to the Commission for assessment' corresponds to the procedural route, which is captured by the variable 'Nature'.

Refute this claim if it can be refuted.

response.objection: The provision governs the procedural steps required before a claim can be assessed, but it does not determine the complexity of the legal procedure itself. The requirement to make a settlement offer is a procedural step, not a measure of complexity.
